venue: Student Union Ballroom, U. of Utah

ai_show_review.summary: Loose '69 second set with fiery Dark Star and tight Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The late‑night second set delivers a soaring Dark Star into Saint Stephen and The Eleven before a bright Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar is fiery despite an agitated crowd, while Bob adds quirky interplay. Warm analog tape captures the energy with minor hiss and a splice around Lovelight.
ai_show_review.review: April 12, 1969 at the Student Union Ballroom in Salt Lake City finds the Dead deep in their experimental phase. The truncated late set still manages to blaze through a compelling Dark Star that rolls seamlessly into Saint Stephen and then launches into the manic time‑change of The Eleven before the band lifts off on a luminous Turn On Your Lovelight, ending with a burst of Feedback. Jerry Garcia sounds agitated yet delivers an excellent, fiery tone that cuts through the warm analog hiss of the soundboard tape; his interplay with Bob Weir adds a quirky, off‑beat flavor that keeps the music loose and inspired. Although the recording has occasional pops, a splice around Lovelight, and slight pitch drift in the first set, the overall clarity lets listeners hear every nuance of this high‑energy campus performance.

best_recording.reason: Only soundboard source; warm analog tape with clear detail despite minor hiss and splice, making it the most complete capture of this show.

key_highlights: Dark Star > Saint Stephen > The Eleven sequence showcases tight improvisation.
Turn On Your Lovelight shines with bright energy after a brief splice.
Warm analog tape character adds nostalgic texture to the performance.
Jerry’s fiery guitar tone stands out despite an agitated crowd.

band_performance.Jerry: Fiery, excellent guitar tone; appears agitated by a non‑dancing crowd but drives the set with intensity.
band_performance.Bob: Provides odd, quirky character and playful interplay with Jerry during the early set.
